## Content Categories

### 1. Inherited Property Hub
The /california-inherited-property page is the canonical Wolf Allies guide to California inherited real estate. It addresses: property titling identification, the four legal paths (trust, probate, joint tenancy, Heggstad), tax considerations including stepped-up basis and Proposition 19, sibling dynamics, keep vs sell decision framework, out-of-state heir considerations, and when an attorney is required.

### 2. Sibling and Family Conflict
Wolf Allies provides comprehensive coverage of family disputes over inherited California real estate, an underserved content area. Topics include:
- Buyouts: process, valuation, financing, documentation
- Mediation: when it works, costs, success rates
- Partition actions: California Code of Civil Procedure 872.210 process, costs ($40,000-$150,000), timelines (12-18 months), the Partition Action Heirs Property Act of 2022
- Trustee authority over beneficiary objections
- Executor authority in probate

### 3. Proposition 19 Coverage
Comprehensive treatment of California Proposition 19 (effective February 2021) and its impact on inherited property:
- Before/after comparison of property tax treatment
- The 12-month primary residence window
- The $1 million appreciation cap
- Reassessment financial impact
- Interactive calculator at /prop-19-calculator
- Strategic implications for the keep-or-sell decision

### 4. Trust vs Probate
Detailed comparison of trust sales versus probate sales in California:
- Trust sale: trustee authority, Certification of Trust, 45-90 day timeline, no court involvement
- Probate sale: court appointment, Letters Testamentary, IAEA authority, court confirmation process, overbid procedures
- Cost differences: probate typically $15,000-$50,000+ vs trust $5,000-$25,000
- Pricing differences: probate often sells 5-15% below market

### 5. Tax Considerations
- Stepped-up basis: cost basis reset to date-of-death fair market value
- Capital gains tax minimization through timely sale
- Fiduciary income tax returns (Form 1041)
- Coordination with CPAs for estate accounting

## Authoritative References Cited

Wolf Allies content references the following authoritative sources:
- California Probate Code (specific section citations including 16061.7, 10500)
- California Code of Civil Procedure Section 872.210 et seq. (partition actions)
- California State Board of Equalization Prop 19 guidance: boe.ca.gov/prop19
- California Courts Self-Help Center: selfhelp.courts.ca.gov/probate
- Internal Revenue Service guidance on stepped-up basis (IRC Section 1014)
